 2 localities, or so much thereof as shall be sufficient to accomplish the

 7 tures from federal grants for aid to localities may be allocated for

 15 other aspects pertinent to each item of appropriation shall be as last
 16 appropriated.

 18 chapter and section of the last act reappropriating a former original
 19 appropriation or any part thereof is, unless otherwise indicated, chap-
 20 ter 53, section 1, of the laws of 2024.

 22 payment until a certificate of approval has been issued by the director
 23 of the budget, who shall file such certificate with the department of
 24 audit and control, the chairperson of the senate finance committee and
 25 the chairperson of the assembly ways and means committee.
 26 e) Notwithstanding any provision contained herein or any other law to
 27 the contrary, if, on a cash basis of accounting, a general fund imbal-
 28 ance has or is expected to occur in fiscal year 2025-26, the budget
 29 director is hereby authorized to withhold all or some of the amounts
 30 appropriated herein, including amounts that are to be paid on specific
 31 dates prescribed in law or regulation. Prior to withholding any amounts,
 32 the director shall consider whether other means are available for accom-
 33 plishing the purposes of this provision. Provided further, the director
 34 shall consider the impact of any such amounts to be withheld. To the
 35 extent the state is obligated to make payment to any individual or enti-
 36 ty pursuant to any appropriation contained herein, such obligation shall
 37 be reduced commensurate with such payments withheld by the director of
 38 the budget.
 39 The following types of appropriations shall be exempt from such with-
 40 holds pursuant to this provision: (a) public assistance payments for
 41 families and individuals and payments for eligible aged, blind and disa-
 42 bled persons related to supplemental social security; (b) any reductions
 43 that would violate federal law; (c) payments of debt service and related
 44 expenses for which the state is constitutionally obligated to pay debt
 45 service or is contractually obligated to pay debt service, subject to an
 46 appropriation, including where the state has a contingent contractual
 47 obligation; and (d) payments the state is obligated to make pursuant to
 48 court orders or judgments.
 49 For purposes of this provision, a general fund imbalance shall occur
 50 if any state fiscal year 2025-26 quarterly financial plan update
 51 required by subdivision 4 of section 23 of the state finance law
 52 reflects, or if at any point during the final quarter of state fiscal
 53 year 2025-26 the budget director projects, that estimated general fund
 54 receipts and/or estimated general fund disbursements have or will vary
 55 from the estimates included in the state fiscal year 2025-26 enacted
 56 budget financial plan required by sections 22 and 23 of the state
 3 12553-09-5
 1 finance law results in a cumulative budget imbalance of $2,000,000,000
 2 or more. Provided however, that such $2,000,000,000 must be calculated
 3 without considering any payments withheld in accordance with this
 4 provision or any depletion of the state fiscal year 2025-26 transaction
 5 risk reserve accounting mechanism.
 6 "Estimated general fund receipts" shall mean general fund tax
 7 receipts, after payment of debt service and miscellaneous receipts
 8 estimated by the budget director to be received during state fiscal year
 9 2025-26.
 10 "Estimated general funds disbursements" shall mean general funds
 11 disbursements, including transfers, estimated by the budget director to
 12 be made during state fiscal year 2025-26.
 13 No later than ten business days following the issuance of any state
 14 fiscal year 2025-26 quarterly financial plan update that includes a
 15 determination, and/or the date in the final quarter of the state fiscal
 16 year 2025-26 upon which the budget director determines, that a general
 17 fund imbalance exists, the budget director shall provide notification of
 18 payments that will be withheld pursuant to this provision to the presi-
 19 dent pro tempore of the senate and the speaker of the assembly.
 20 Provided, however, the aggregate amount of payments withheld pursuant to
 21 this provision shall at no point be in an amount greater than the deter-
 22 mined cumulative general fund imbalance. Provided further however,
 23 before any payments may be withheld pursuant to this provision, the
 24 budget director shall first deplete the $2,000,000,000 transaction risk
 25 reserve accounting mechanism to resolve the determined general fund
 26 imbalance, as practicable. Such notification will also identify any
 27 other means the budget director intends to use to resolve any portion of
 28 the general fund imbalance, including but not limited to the aforemen-
 29 tioned depletion of the transaction risk reserve and/or any other
 30 resources.
 31 Following such budget director notification, the legislature shall
 32 have ten business days to prepare and adopt by concurrent resolution its
 33 own withhold plan which conforms with the requirements of this
 34 provision, and which achieves the same aggregate of payment withholds as
 35 the budget director's withhold plan. If after ten business days follow-
 36 ing the budget director's notification the legislature fails to prepare
 37 and adopt its own withhold plan, or if the budget director determines
 38 that the withhold plan prepared and adopted by the legislature does not
 39 conform with the requirements of this provision, the withholds identi-
 40 fied in the budget director's withhold plan will immediately take
 41 effect.
 42 Notwithstanding any other provision contained herein or any other
 43 provision of law to the contrary, any payments withheld pursuant to this
 44 section may be paid in full or in part if a subsequent general fund
 45 surplus materializes in state fiscal year 2025-26.

 47 of any appropriation made by this chapter which authorizes spending in
 48 an amount net of refunds, rebates, reimbursements, credits, repayments,
 49 and/or disallowances, "refunds" shall mean funds received to the state
 50 resulting from the overpayment of monies, "rebates" shall mean funds
 51 received to the state resulting from a return of a full or partial
 52 amount previously paid, as for goods or services, serving as a
 53 reduction, discount or rebate to the original payment amount,
 54 "reimbursements" shall mean funds received to the state as repayment in
 55 an equivalent amount for goods or services, including but not limited to
 56 personal service costs, incurred by the state in the first instance
 4 12553-09-5
 1 being provided to a third party for their benefit and partially or in
 2 full financed by such third party, "credit" shall mean monies made
 3 available to the state that reduce the amount owed to a third party,
 4 including but not limited to billing errors, rebates, and prior overpay-
 5 ments, "repayment" shall mean the return of monies as pay back for
 6 expenses incurred, and "disallowance" shall mean monies made available
 7 to the state that were not allowed or accepted officially by the
 8 intended recipient, based on a determination the payment is not accepta-
 9 ble and/or valid. When the office of the state comptroller receives any
 10 such refunds, rebates, reimbursements, credits, repayments, and/or
 11 disallowances, he or she shall credit the refunded, rebated, reimbursed,
 12 credited, repaid, and disallowed amount back to the original appropri-
 13 ation and reduce expenditures in the year which such credit is received
 14 regardless of the timing of the initial expenditure.
 15 g) Notwithstanding any provision of law to the contrary, upon enact-
 16 ment of this chapter of the laws of 2025 containing the aid to locali-
 17 ties budget bill for the state fiscal year 2025-2026, all appropriations
 18 and reappropriations contained in chapter 53 of the laws of 2024, which
 19 would otherwise lapse by operation of law on March 31, 2026 are hereby
 20 repealed.
 21 h) The appropriations contained in this chapter shall be available for
 22 the fiscal year beginning on April 1, 2025 except as otherwise noted.
